description: The graph illustrates the performance of various dense retrieval methods, measured by MRR@10, as a function of the number of queries used during inference, ranging from 1 to 10. The x-axis, labeled "Number of queries used during inference (S)," is linear with integer values from 1 to 10. The y-axis, labeled "MRR@10," ranges from 33.0 to 36.5, with major gridlines at intervals of 0.5. Six distinct methods are compared: DPR w/o query (black solid line), DPR w/ gold (yellow with circular markers), DPR w/ top-1 (green with circular markers), DPR w/ bottom-1 (purple with circular markers), DPR w/ random (blue with circular markers), and DPR w/ curriculum (red with circular markers). The DPR w/ curriculum method consistently achieves the highest MRR@10, starting at approximately 35.1 and increasing to about 35.7. The DPR w/ gold method shows a steady increase from near 33.0 to around 35.0. The DPR w/ top-1 method begins at 33.0 and rises sharply to 36.5. The DPR w/ bottom-1 method remains relatively flat around 34.6. The DPR w/ random method starts at 34.8 and slightly increases to 35.1. The DPR w/o query method is a flat horizontal line at approximately 34.6. The legend is positioned in the lower right corner of the plot.
